title: R' Yaakov Armenaya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman gives one occurrence, in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 6:5: Rav Nachman said in the name of R’ Yaakov Armenaya, “What is a question for R’ Elazar is clear to R’ Yose bar Chanina.” Hyman suggests that the title might instead be R’ Nachman, who is mentioned several times in the Jerusalem Talmud.

notes.text: Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 6:5 reads Rabbi Shimon where the supplied notice has Rabbi Elazar, and explicitly names Rabbi Yose bar Chanina. Hyman’s proposed Rav-to-Rabbi correction concerns Nachman, not Yaakov. The Elazar/Shimon discrepancy remains open.

The saved whole Mechon-Mamre Gittin6:5 scalar reads Rav Nachman reporting abbreviated R' Yaakov Armenaya, with Eliezer and Yose bar Chanina. Eliezer differs from supplied Elazar and from the inherited Venice/Guggenheimer Shimon comparison; none is silently harmonized. Hyman tentatively proposes that Nachman’s title should read R', not a new Yaakov or a reversal of the question. These exact personal titles are abbreviated in the named paragraph, so full Rabbi expansions are withdrawn. Armenaya remains a transliteration, not a new ethnic or place identity. פ״א means once, not chapter1.

The printed Hyman page gives Rav Nachman and R’ Elazar. The Mechon Mamre text gives Rav Nachman and Eliezer, while Guggenheimer’s Hebrew gives Rabbi Nachman and Shimon. The Rashba’s commentary on Gittin 66a, in the Gerlitz digital edition, quotes Rabbi Nachman in the name of Rabbi Yaakov Admoni, with Elazar and Yose bar Chanina. The forms are reported as readings of this passage. Hyman’s proposal concerns Nachman’s title.
